_[How to write this description](.github/pull-requests.md)_

## 🎯 Summary

<!-- One or two sentences. Technical terms are fine — this is the abstract, not marketing
copy. What it adds or changes, the route or boundary it lives behind, and any piece you had
to add to make it work. No version numbers and no image digests: they move on their own and
rot in prose. -->

## 🔎 What to review

<!-- Where a mistake would matter, and what correct looks like — two to four bullets. Not
a file list; the diff already has the files. Delete only when the change is trivial. -->

## 🔑 Key decisions

<!-- One ### per decision, titled with the decision itself so a reviewer can skim the
headings and stop at the one they disagree with. **Why** is the constraint in two or three
sentences, not the story. **Usage** is the evidence: counts, precedent, upstream default,
or that there is none. Rejections and deferrals belong here too, in the same shape — there
is no separate list. Delete the section when nothing here is arguable. -->

### <The decision, as a statement>

**Why:** <the constraint that forces it>
**Usage:** <what other people do, or "first here">

## ⚠️ Beware

<!-- Anything to be aware of before this lands: a manual step Flux cannot do (a value only
the owner can supply, a directory on the NAS, a DNS record), or behaviour that is
irreversible or destructive. Delete the section when there is nothing. Never write a line
saying there is nothing to beware of — an empty reassurance is noise. -->

## 🔗 Related

<!-- Only when applicable: Closes #123, depends on #456, or the stack order. -->
